BBC report (26 March 2026): India's parliament passed a bill amending the 2019 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act that removes the right to self-identify, limits recognition to biological/physical traits certified by medical boards and district authorities, and mandates certification for gender-affirming surgery; protests followed and a Supreme Court-appointed panel called the change a setback to the 2014 self-identification ruling. National framework applying equally to this island union territory.

Times of India city report (18 August 2024): a transwoman alleged a railway-police constable groped her as a 'gender check' at a Kolkata metro station; the police denied it and filed a counter-FIR — shared national evidence that security forces treat trans presentation as grounds for invasive identity verification at transport checkpoints, a practice relevant wherever such checkpoints exist.
